title_formula_note: Chosen: the CD's working title (brief section 1, re-approved in decisions.md 2026-10-22). New family T12 'When Earth Had [vanished extreme] That [revelation clause]', borrowed as a frame from Mr. Science's 'When Earth Had/Was X' engine (Supermountains 3.39M, Antarctica Jungle 4.82M); never used by us, and it breaks the 'Why/How/Would' openers of 021-024. Rule check: (1) 55 chars, 11 words; (2) Title Case, no caps words, emoji, ! or ?; (3) 'When Earth Had' frame plus revelation clause (logged as T12 for formula tracking, like T7-T11); (4) one death verb 'Kill', no dread adjective; (5) revelation clause 'That Bugs Could Kill Doug'; (6) no 'in N Minutes', no leading count; (7) the brief's thumbnail text 'TOO MUCH AIR' repeats the title word 'Much', so the thumbnail brief proposes 'AIR DID THIS' instead; (9) 5 candidates; (10) not a Paint Explainer title or noun swap, and not Mr. Science's wording. CD constraints: oxygen stays the named cause; no 'hunted'/'attacked'; no 'Bugs That Killed...'. 'Could Kill Doug' keeps it Doug's cartoon premise, not a claim that bugs killed people. Honesty: bugs kill Doug at 207, 208, 210 (and 206 indirectly), and death 204 is the oxygen itself (the fire), so 'so much oxygen' literally kills Doug on screen; the boss segment says honestly that oxygen 'may have helped, but nobody can yet say how much' (Cambridge 2021, Snelling et al. 2026 Nature). Alternates: (T12) the CD-approved short form, closest A/B to the lead; (T4) revelation 'That Grew Up Breathing Extra Oxygen' (juxtaposition, no causal over-claim; echoes the script's 'Everything on this list grew up breathing this air'); (T4) revelation 'Scientists Still Can't Fully Explain' (honest to the on-air oxygen debate; the curiosity A/B with no Doug); (T9 'Why...' family) death verb 'Dying', scope 'Earth's High-Oxygen Age', Doug-first. Rejected: brief lead 'Why Bugs Got Deadlier the More Oxygen Earth Had' (states oxygen as the settled cause of size, which the script's 2026 Nature resolution contradicts), 'The Scariest Bugs That Ever Lived Were the Size of Doug' (no oxygen, and only items 7-9 reach Doug size), any 'Weirdest'/'Craziest', T1 and T2 wording, 'the Deeper Doug Goes'.

description:
About 300 million years ago Earth's air held a lot more oxygen than today's, and giant bugs filled the coal forests: a sea scorpion as big as a person, a griffinfly with a wingspan of about 70 centimetres, and Arthropleura, the largest land arthropod known. Doug goes back to meet the Carboniferous giants, smallest to biggest, and finds out how much of it the oxygen really explains.

Which prehistoric world should Doug visit next? Tell us in the comments.
